_README: Started by init.py from Pole Position II (NTSC) (Atari) (1987) (A85FB962).a78.
Every human judgement about this ROM lives in this file; the
generated listings are disposable, so renaming is free.
What to do next, roughly in order:
1. python tools/disasm.py Pole Position II (NTSC) (Atari) (1987) (A85FB962).a78 -c annotations.json
Read the coverage it reports. Low coverage is normal at
first and is the number you are trying to move.
2. Every unresolved indirect jump it reports is a hole. Add the
target to `entries`, or the pointer pair to `ram_vectors` if
the handler is installed into RAM.
3. python tools/audiotrace.py Pole Position II (NTSC) (Atari) (1987) (A85FB962).a78 -c annotations.json
Finds the sound code and the tables feeding it.
4. Name things in `labels` as soon as you know what they are.
See docs/method.md for the working order and docs/pitfalls.md for
the traps that each cost real time.

blocks.name: dat_StateHandlersHi
blocks.note: High bytes of the state dispatch table; see dat_StateHandlersLo at rom:A7C2. States 2/16, 3/17, 4/5 and 6/7 share handlers.

blocks.name: dat_TrackNames
blocks.note: Track names as text: TEST, FUJI, SEASIDE, each followed by a digit and a $B0 separator; SUZUKA sits apart at $A4A4. Finding these is what proved J/K/Z live at $B1-$B3 rather than being absent from the font -- see docs/FINDINGS.md, including the retraction of the claim that these names were graphics.

blocks.name: dat_SegLengths
blocks.note: The segment-length menu: fourteen 16-bit lengths, low bytes at $A197 and high bytes at $A1A5. Read as pairs they are round decimal numbers -- 300, 500, 900, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000, 5000, 5300, 10000, 1200, 600, 800 -- which is what identifies them; the road accumulates the pair as a 16-bit quantity at rom:C4E7. LoadTrack indexes this by the LOW nibble of each track byte.

blocks.name: dat_DliHandlerTable
blocks.note: The display-interrupt handler table, found live then read statically. The NMI entry at rom:EBEF indexes TWO PARALLEL TABLES by ram_00FF -- low bytes at $A48A, high bytes at $A496, twelve entries -- builds the vector in ram_00FD/FE and does JMP (ram_00FD) at rom:EC06. Eleven targets are in ROM and are now entries; index 0 is $2456, which is RAM, so that handler is code copied there at run time and cannot be reached statically. This table is the first structure identified inside the 16,805-byte block at $8000, and it was found because --check-gaps flagged the indirect jump rather than letting it pass.

blocks.name: dat_SndStreamPtrs
blocks.note: Four parallel 20-byte tables, indexed by sound id: pitch stream low at $A558 and high at $A56C (loaded by SoundPitchPtr rom:E03E), waveform stream low at $A580 and high at $A594 (loaded at rom:E020). Each sound has three INDEPENDENT byte streams -- pitch to AUDF, waveform to AUDC, volume to AUDV -- advanced by their own per-voice indices SndPitchIdx, SndAudcIdx and SndAudvIdx.

blocks.name: dat_StateHandlersLo
blocks.note: Low bytes of the main game-state dispatch table, twenty entries. sub_D253 at rom:D25E indexes this and dat_StateHandlersHi by the state in $9D, builds the vector in $40/$41 and does JMP ($0040) at rom:D26A. The tracer cannot follow that, so sixteen of the twenty handlers sat in gaps -- several landing exactly on a gap start address, which is what confirmed the table. Entry 11 is rom:D3F7, QualifyingPosition, which had already been identified independently. Entry 20 reads $00AA, out of ROM, so the table is exactly twenty long.

blocks.name: dat_HudSpeedTemplate
blocks.note: The SPEED field's template, copied to ram_1FBA by rom:F204. Reads 'SPEED  00' then $AC $AD, which render as the 'mph' unit on screen.

blocks.name: dat_AccelCurves
blocks.note:
Two 16-entry acceleration curves, indexed at rom:C2F6 by (Speed >> 4) + Gear, where Gear is 0 for LO and $10 for HI. Entries are signed and ADDED to Speed at rom:C33A.

LO  03 05 07 08 07 06 05 04 03 02 00 00 FF FF FE FC
HI  01 01 01 02 03 05 07 06 05 04 03 02 01 01 01 01

LO pulls hardest at index 3 (speed 48-63) and then goes NEGATIVE from index 12, actively braking the car above about 192 -- so LO has a top speed near 176. HI barely moves the car off the line at +1 but never stops pulling, which is the only way to reach the 255 the HUD tops out at. That is the real Pole Position gearbox, in sixteen bytes each.

blocks.name: dat_TrackStreamPtrs
blocks.note: Four 4-byte tables, so four tracks: stream A pointer low at $C955 and high at $C959, stream B pointer low at $C95D and high at $C961. LoadTrack rom:D917 indexes all four by TrackIndex ($C4) and puts the results in $40/$41 and $42/$43. Lengths come from $AAD4 (stream A) and $A4AA (stream B), and the initial object cursor from $ABD4. This sixteen-byte range was an unexplained gap until the loader was read.

blocks.name: dat_SkidThresholds
blocks.note: Eight traction thresholds, indexed by Speed >> 5 (rom:C269 shifts right five times, so 0-7 across the whole speed range): 24, 24, 22, 20, 19, 18, 16, 14. SkidCheck skids the car when |LateralVel - RoadCurve| reaches the threshold for the current speed band, so the faster the car is going the less divergence it takes to break traction.

blocks.name: dat_HudTemplates
blocks.note: The HUD text, copied into the display buffer by rom:F204: $C976 (19 bytes) -> ram_1F8A, $C98A (19) -> ram_1FA8, $C9A2 (11) -> ram_1F9D, and dat_AE24 (11) -> ram_1FBA. Decoding these against the labels on screen -- TOP, SCORE, LAP, SPEED -- is what gave the character set.

blocks.name: dat_D3A0
blocks.note: Four bytes, 01 05 09 0D -- an arithmetic sequence, step 4, so a small index or offset table rather than code. Flagged by --check-gaps as a gap stepped over by rom:D39D JMP $D713, which is the shape that hid the physics at rom:D701; decoding it by hand settled it as data. Nothing traced references it yet, so which routine indexes it is still open.

blocks.name: dat_QualifyThresholds
blocks.note: The eight qualifying thresholds, as TWO PARALLEL TABLES: dat_DBA0 holds the seconds and dat_DBA8 the hundredths, both BCD, indexed by position 0-7. rom:D3F7 walks them comparing LapTimeSeconds then LapTimeHundredths, stopping at the first the lap beats. Reads 58.50, 60.00, 62.00, 64.00, 66.00, 68.00, 70.00, 73.00 seconds -- the manual gives only the first and last of those and both match. Searching for the pair 58 50 as adjacent bytes finds nothing, because it is split across the two tables eight bytes apart.

blocks.name: dat_SndVolPtrs
blocks.note: Volume-envelope stream pointers, low at $E049 and high at $E05D, twenty entries; loaded at rom:E008 and read into AUDV. Third of the three streams per sound -- see dat_SndStreamPtrs at rom:A558.

blocks.name: dat_SndDurations
blocks.note: Frames per step for each of the twenty sounds, read at rom:DF65 into SndDuration. Ranges from 1 (the engine and the short effects) to 64 (sound $09).

blocks.name: dat_SndPriority
blocks.note: Priority per sound id, consulted by SoundStart at rom:DF0A when both voices are busy: the incoming sound takes a voice only if it outranks what is already there. The scheme is legible at a glance -- the engine $0F is priority 0, so anything at all steals its voice, and the race-start fanfare $13 is priority 20, far above the 2-10 of everything else, so nothing interrupts it. NOTE the last byte at $E1DE is also the first note of the pitch stream for sound 3; both want the value $14, so the tables abut and share it.

blocks.name: dat_PerspectiveZHi
blocks.note: High bytes of the 78-entry perspective table. ObjectCollision at rom:C86E walks Y from $4D down, subtracting this and dat_PerspectiveZLo from the object 16-bit Z distance, to find the screen row an object at that distance draws on. Read as a pair with the low table at rom:EB56; note the high table sits at the LOWER address. Also used from rom:CC68, rom:CE42 and rom:CECD.

blocks.name: dat_PerspectiveZLo
blocks.note: Low bytes of the 78-entry perspective table; see dat_PerspectiveZHi at rom:EAB9.
